transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Lee (Redwood SE), Daniel Reed (CISO - Ironwood), Aisha Khan (Head of Ops - Ironwood), Marcus Li (SRE - Ironwood), Priya Desai (Procurement - Ironwood)

Summary (auto): quick review of BC/DR, incident response, SLA, escalation paths, and integration points. Action items captured.

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, i'm maya from redwood, i'm the AE on this account, joined by connor our se. can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Daniel Reed: yeah daniel reed, ciso at ironwood bank. focusing on policy and compliance.
[00:17] Aisha Khan: aisha, ops. we run the production stacks and oncall triage.
[00:21] Marcus Li: marcus, s r e, i handle infra and runbooks.
[00:25] Priya Desai: priya, procurement - i'll be collecting docs and legal bits.
[00:30] Connor Lee: hi, connor lee, se, i mainly cover runtime, sla, and incident response details.

[02:05] Maya Patel: cool, the agenda for today - quick SOC2/ISO recaps, then deep into incident response & b c d r targets rto/rpo, how we measure uptime, and the escalation process. we'll also cover s s o, rb a c, audit logs and kms notes as they tie into incident handling.

[03:20] Daniel Reed: perfect. our baseline ask: we need documented rto and rpo commitments, and an escalation matrix with SLAs for notification and remediation. previously we've seen vendors list 99.9% but not define runbooks. looking for clear playbooks and evidence of testing.

[04:10] Connor Lee: totally, yes. to be clear, redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private (vpc) modes; rto/rpo behavior differs a bit by deployment. for hosted api, our recovery for infra-level failures typically: incident detection -> failover -> restore kv cache and containers. typical rto we've documented for hosted is 15-30 minutes for control-plane incidents, but for catastrophic data-plane we target rto up to 60 minutes depending on severity and model state. rpo depends on caching and streaming sessions; default rpo for hosted is one hour for persisted data; for private deployments customers can tighten these with replication config.

[05:00] Aisha Khan: okay, 15-30 minutes is reasonable for control-plane. for us we need p1 rto under 30 minutes and rpo under 1 hour. is that something you can commit to in an sla for dedicated or private?

[05:32] Connor Lee: yes, for dedicated pools we can commit to 30 minute rto for P1 with active standby in a different AZ, and rpo down to 15 minutes if you enable cross-az replication on the model KV cache; that is an opt-in config and has cost impact. i'll note that.

[06:10] Daniel Reed: can you define severity? how do you classify P1 vs P2? also what are notification timelines?

[06:30] Maya Patel: quick read: our standard severity definitions - P1: complete service outage impacting production traffic; P2: partial degradation with elevated errors or latency; P3: single-customer or low-impact issues. notification SLA: initial ack within 15 minutes for P1, 1 hour for P2. full incident summary within 24-48 hours. these are in our standard SLA but we can tweak for enterprise contracts.

[07:50] Marcus Li: what's escalation look like? pager, slack, phone? we need an escalation matrix that maps to our oncall and our vendor contacts.

[08:05] Connor Lee: yes, matrix: level 1 - infra oncall engineer (automated alert), level 2 - se oncall, level 3 - engineering manager and platform lead, level 4 - exec oncall and account team. notifications via pagerduty (we integrate), email and a dedicated slack channel are options. we can add phone bridge for severity1. also support 24/7 oncall for enterprise.

[09:20] Aisha Khan: do you have runbook examples you can share? and do you do RTO tests / DR drills?

[09:35] Connor Lee: yes we have a runbook library. i'll share redacted runbooks — they include play-by-play detection, triage, mitigation, rollback and postmortem steps. on drills: yes, we do quarterly simulated failover tests for dedicated customers or yearly for hosted unless requested otherwise — we can run an exec tabletop with your team.

[11:00] Daniel Reed: logs and auditability are huge for us. can you describe audit log retention, who can access them, and whether we get raw logs or a portal?

[11:22] Maya Patel: logs: we provide per-tenant audit logs with an API export and exports to SIEMs (splunk, sumo, datadog). retention defaults to 90 days for audit trails, longer retention is an enterprise add-on. RBAC controls who can access logs; we tie into your SAML provider (okta) and map groups to roles. logs include user actions, key changes, and admin API calls.

[12:30] Marcus Li: retention of 90 days is okay but we may need 1 year for certain trails for compliance. is that available?

[12:45] Maya Patel: yes, 1 year retention is available as an add-on, we can include export workflows to your s3 or an on-prem endpoint.

[13:10] Priya Desai: procurement question - what SLAs for uptime do you publish and what are the credit structures?

[13:25] Connor Lee: our baseline hosted SLA is 99.95% monthly for API availability; dedicated SLA can be 99.97% or higher depending on contract. credits scale with downtime windows — typical: <99.95% gets 10% service credit, lower tiers get more; exact banding is in the SLA doc. we'll share the draft.

[14:35] Daniel Reed: what's your measurement window? do you exclude scheduled maintenance?

[14:45] Connor Lee: measurement is monthly; planned maintenance is typically excluded if notified 72 hours in advance and scheduled in maintenance windows. emergency maintenance may be treated differently; all that is in the contract.

[15:30] Aisha Khan: encryption and key mgmt — do you use customer-managed keys? hsm?

[15:45] Maya Patel: yes, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and BYOK flows; for on-prem or high-assurance customers we support HSM integrations and do key custody with split control options. all data is encrypted at rest and in transit (tls 1.2+), and we have envelope encryption for model artifacts.

[16:55] Marcus Li: if we want BYOK, does that change your incident process — e.g., can you do emergency key rotation and how do backups work without access to customer keys?

[17:10] Connor Lee: good q. with BYOK we cannot decrypt without your key; for emergency rotation we coordinate with the customer's security team. backups of encrypted blobs are stored but inaccessible without keys. that impacts the restore timelines so we document it in the runbook and recommend key rotation windows planned in advance.

[18:40] Daniel Reed: data residency — we need all data kept in us-east-1 for now. is that a private deployment?

[18:55] Maya Patel: you can do hosted with region restriction (we can pin tenancy to us-east-1), or we can do private VPC deployment in your account. for strict controls we recommend private (VPC) or dedicated single-az with placement. we'll capture exact requirements in the SOW.

[20:05] Marcus Li: curious about incident postmortem and forensics — do you provide packet level info? full traces? how deep do the logs go?

[20:20] Connor Lee: our audit trails include API request/response metadata, model invocation traces (not model payload by default unless enabled), and system metrics. for deep forensics we can provide expanded traces and raw logs via secure export; packet captures are not typically available unless we've done a co-located support engagement, but we provide network flow logs and platform metrics.

[22:00] Aisha Khan: how do you handle escalations outside business hours? we need 24/7 support and a clear contact path.

[22:15] Maya Patel: enterprise packages include 24/7 support; escalation goes through pagerduty -> phone bridge -> exec oncall if not acknowledged within defined window. we'll include SLA ack windows and an escalation matrix in the docs we share.

[24:10] Daniel Reed: can you walk through a recent P1 incident and show timelines? helps us trust the process.

[24:25] Connor Lee: sure, we shared a redacted postmortem earlier — quick example: incident detected 02:07, auto-alert at 02:09, oncall ack at 02:12, mitigation started 02:18 (traffic re-route), full service restored 02:34. postmortem published 36 hours later with root cause and action items. i'll attach that redacted PM.

[26:50] Marcus Li: that timeline looks good. do you have runbooks that map to those timestamps so we can practice drills?

[27:05] Connor Lee: yes, runbooks include checklists with expected times for each step. we can coordinate a tabletop and execute a failover in a staging window to validate RTOs.

[28:30] Aisha Khan: our legal team will want specific language on notification windows and credit calculations. procurement will review.

[28:45] Priya Desai: yep, i'll need SOC2 and ISO artifacts + SLA draft. also any pen test reports.

[29:05] Maya Patel: we'll share SOC2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, the recent pentest summary, the SLA draft, and runbook examples. connor will attach the runbook and escalation matrix.

[30:20] Daniel Reed: one more - do you provide a dedicated customer success / ops contact during onboarding to help configure replication and DR?

[30:35] Maya Patel: yes onboarding includes a solutions engineer and a customer success manager to help with replication, config, and runbook alignment. we can add a dedicated post-sales technical lead for the first 90 days.

[32:10] Marcus Li: about metrics — how do you measure rto/rpo for reporting? do we get an automated report?

[32:22] Connor Lee: we emit incident telemetry in our console and can push incident timelines and MTTR/MTTA metrics to your SIEM or a secure s3 export. monthly SLA reports are standard for enterprise.

[33:40] Aisha Khan: timeline to get everything in contract? we need internal signoff by end of q1; procurement wants legal terms and insurance proofs.

[33:55] Maya Patel: typical cycle is 3-6 weeks for enterprise SOW and SLA negotiation. for faster timelines we can provision a pilot with terms on a temporary contract while legal finishes.

[35:10] Daniel Reed: small nit — our compliance team insists on MFA & SAML for admin, and role separation for dev vs ops.

[35:25] Connor Lee: supported — we have RBAC roles (admin, ops, auditor, dev) and SAML/Sso (okta) with enforced MFA for admin roles. we can provide a sample provisioning SAML integration guide.

[36:40] Priya Desai: any vendor insurance requirements? we need cyber insurance limits and attestations.

[36:55] Maya Patel: we carry cyber liability; i'll include insurer and limit details in the packet. also SOC2 & ISO help with underwriters.

[38:10] Marcus Li: if we do private deployment, does the incident handoff differ? e.g., do you have remote runbooks or local ops?

[38:25] Connor Lee: for private deployments we run a control plane that coordinates with your infra; runbooks are collaborative. in many cases the customer's ops team will execute containment and we provide guidance and escalation. we can provide a hybrid model if you prefer full runbook ownership on your side.

[40:00] Daniel Reed: good. let's talk about documentation delivery and timelines.

[40:12] Maya Patel: action items recap — i'll send SOC2/ISO/pentest; connor will send runbook and proposed escalation matrix and rto test plan; we'll schedule a tabletop drill with your team next week if that works.

[41:00] Aisha Khan: next week should work, we'll pick slots. please include expected duration for the tabletop.

[41:12] Connor Lee: tabletop usually 90 minutes with a follow-up 60 minute technical re-run if needed.

[42:20] Daniel Reed: okay, thanks everyone. any final q's?

[42:25] Priya Desai: none from procurement.
[42:27] Marcus Li: all good.

[42:40] Maya Patel: great, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites. thanks all.

[43:00] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript has minor auto-caption errors (e.g., "S0C2" or "K-V cache" may appear). attachments referenced: redacted postmortem pdf (link shared in chat), SOC2 Type II report link, ISO 27001 cert link, draft SLA doc (link), runbook examples (link).
